mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.25% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.25% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for four consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive two-quarter decline in real GDP (GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes of two consecutive quarterly GDP declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals persistent supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and lowers profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of six consecutive months of INDPRO contraction relative to its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of at least 2% in both the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) and Real Personal Income (RSAFS) over three months signals a robust residential demand recovery, which boosts construction and related equities, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise by at least 2% over three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and RSAFS rise by at least 2% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months, it signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to consider rate hikes, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 0.5% MoM for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months with CPIAUCSL > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month is contradictory and signals a data anomaly or revision shock, which historically precedes abnormal S&P 500 volatility and negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both increase by at least 0.4pp MoM in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE and PAYEMS increase by at least 0.4pp MoM simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in Real Personal Income (RSAFS) above 0.4% for eight consecutive months signals sustained household demand growth, which supports consumer discretionary spending and boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of eight consecutive months with RSAFS > 0.4% growth.
